doc.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998

title: First record date with Leonard Feather
summary: She recalls the Black and White session with Feather on piano, Georgie Auld, Barney Bigard and a drummer, and later labels.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Now when your first opportunity to record came up, you had kind of an interesting, if my facts are correct, it was kind of an interesting combination of people. Was it Leonard Feather?

Yeah, the pianist didn’t show up so Leonard Feather had to play piano. And it was Georgie Auld on tenor, and it was, the bassist was, his son is named Pickles, I can’t think of his name right now. But it was all top notch musicians, and Georgie Auld on tenor and clarinet was —
Yeah Barney Bigard, yeah, help me.
Barney Bigard. And drums was Stan Levy? Did you know Stan Levy?
And I can’t think of the bass player. A very well known bass player too.
He’s always a good guess because he played on so many records, you know you’ve got a 50 percent chance. And this was for what label? Or was it for a label?
Oh, Black and White. It was for Black and White. And then I got a chance to record with National and RCA Victor and I think Decca. Some of them I’ve forgotten the labels I was on.
